title: The Discovery Journal — A year in which AI proposes, the computer calculates, the proof judges and humans decide what it means
description:
A book for everyone, no scientific background needed: one year of work (May to October 2026) by an engineer and AI agents, told simply, with pictures and pencil-and-paper examples. It follows a single thread: AI proposes, calculation explores, a computer-checked proof (Lean 4) judges, and humans decide what it means. This is the Elenchus method, which gives every claim a confidence level: A (the judge, a program, looked at every step), L (written in the literature), C (reasoning nobody checked by machine), X (a numerical sketch).

Contents. Twenty contributions chosen by a rubric fixed in advance and applied the same way across all fields (mathematics, physics, cosmology, population genetics, numerics, AI methodology), each told in the same form: the idea in one picture, what was done, how we made sure it is not wrong, what it does not say. Three are lessons (an expectation overturned by calculation). Also included: the Elenchus chapter, the path to neuro-symbolic science, a little dictionary, the list of claims we withdrew, and five hidden pictures.

Honesty. All results were produced by AI agents (Claude) under the author's direction and audited by other AI agents; no human mathematician has reviewed them. Several rely on openai/math theorems, also AI-generated and not peer reviewed. The Sandier–Serfaty conjecture is not proved here, no Clay problem is solved, and the book also tells the year's mistakes and retractions. Private repositories are described only in broad terms. Independent audit: ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS, corrections applied; translated from the French edition by AI agents, with a fidelity check.

Dedicated to my family.
notes: English edition, v1, translated from the French edition. Selection: rubric frozen (RUBRIC.md) before scoring, 113 candidates, 20 selected; scores and justifications are in the supporting bundle. Code and figures: AutoevolveAI papers/discovery_journal_2026_en.
